analysis.title: Mega-Cap Tech Tries To Stay "Duration Resistant"; Goldman Says Brace For A "Spirited Q4 In The Shooting Gallery"
key_insights: Pasquariello (GS head of hedge fund coverage) says 'three down, one to go' and tells traders to prepare for a spirited Q4. S&P is holding up despite pressure across global bond markets, and NDX just made a higher high.
Q3 performance was highly dispersed: Magnificent Seven +11%, cap-weighted S&P +2%, equal-weight S&P -2%, Russell -8%. The US 10-year yield rose 82 bps over the quarter.
Equal-weight S&P is down seven straight weeks. Pasquariello says this can be read as poor breadth or as evidence that cap-weighted S&P, led by US mega-cap tech, is hard to beat.
Leaders are leading on strong earnings growth and laggards are lagging because of higher rates and oil. Momentum was volatile: -30% in July, -14% in August, +27% in September.

NDX has risen in 11 of the past 13 days despite higher rates. Pasquariello attributes this to fundamental news flow at the largest companies. September was the one part of the market where capital clearly flowed in.

Single-stock drivers cited: META +25% over the past month on agentic AI for consumers, MU rallied on strong earnings despite a large market cap and high multiple, and NVDA added $150bn to its buyback for a $235bn total, with nearly $300bn of market cap added since.

Asia: a GS colleague notes parts of the global investment community remain underweight a region where some of the largest companies have sell-side price targets implying ~90% upside. Japan: TOPIX +20.0% YTD in local terms vs ~11.8% for the S&P, Nikkei +36.6%.
Europe: Pasquariello doubts European equities can compete with US and Asian equities in the next round, given pressure on EU sovereign debt.
Iran/Oil: lots of talk and no progress, with the temperature possibly rising. Persian Gulf oil exports are back to the 2025 average, so the oil market has adapted to the situation.

Q4 technical setup is constructive: quarter-end and month-end supply is largely behind us, long-only and levered funds have shed length, buybacks should accelerate as Q3 reporting proceeds, and US retail investors were inactive in September. S&P has been stuck near 7700.

Foreign investors are still buying US equities despite de-dollarization calls. Global 10-year yields, including US and Japan, are rising while US mega-cap tech makes higher highs. The key Q4 question is whether these stocks stay 'duration resistant'.

The ZeroHedge commentary says the market has picked a winner within the rise in rates: a few cash-flow-rich companies. It describes the rally as narrow, with violent momentum swings, and as better for the index than for the median stock.

Rising global bond yields, especially US and Japanese 10-year yields, and pressure on EU sovereign debt.
Mega-cap tech could stop being 'duration resistant', and no second engine of leadership is visible.

tension_points.bull_case: Mega-cap tech is rising on earnings growth and buybacks, such as NVDA's $235bn plan, with NDX up in 11 of 13 days despite higher rates. Length has been shed, quarter-end supply is done and buybacks reopen, so 7700 could be a pause before higher highs.
tension_points.bear_case: Breadth is poor, with equal-weight S&P down seven weeks and the Russell down 8% in Q3 as the 10-year rose 82 bps. If mega-cap tech stops being duration-resistant there is no second engine, since Europe, Asia and oil offer no alternative leadership.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Mega-cap tech ceasing to be 'duration resistant' as global yields keep rising.
